### Before upgrading: update every host to v0.7.0

This release adds host icons and colours to what hosts share with each other. v0.7.0
cannot pair or switch with v0.6.x or earlier, so update every computer sharing the
display to v0.7.0. The pairing password and settings are kept; there is no need to pair
again.

### A new interface

The whole app has a new design: translucent glass panels, the system fonts, and reworked
light and dark appearances.

- **The switch center shows every shared display at once.** Each display is drawn showing
  the host it is on, with one key per host below it; press one to switch.
- **Many displays or hosts open as a matrix.** With three or more shared displays or four
  or more hosts, the switch center is a display-by-host table: a cell switches one display,
  and "Switch all" in a column head switches every display. The toggle in the top right
  moves between Displays and Matrix, and the app remembers the choice.
- **Settings are split into tabs:** Displays, Hosts & Pairing, Shortcut & Startup,
  Appearance & Language, Help & Diagnostics, and Reset. The language and appearance menus
  move from the sidebar to Appearance & Language.
- **Renaming and reordering hosts move to Hosts & Pairing.** Drag a host or use the arrows
  to reorder it, and the pencil to rename it; this computer is in the same list.
- **Input notes become port tiles.** Each port shows which host uses it, and its note is
  written right in the tile.
- Saving from another tab while a field is invalid now opens the tab that field is on.

### Host icons and colours

On Settings › Hosts & Pairing, click the icon beside a host to choose one of twelve icons
and ten colours — gaming, server, work, home and more. The choice applies at once to the
switch center, the matrix and the host switcher, and reaches every paired host like the
host's name; a host that was offline catches up the next time it connects. "Use default"
returns to the look chosen by platform and host order.

### Host switcher

- It is now a list, and the **digit keys 1–9** switch straight to a host.
- With more than one shared display, **Tab** chooses between every display and a single
  one. Switching every display runs one display at a time and shows each one's progress.
- If some displays fail to switch, the switcher re-reads where everything is, so trying
  again only goes after the ones that failed.

### Quick switch from the tray and menu bar

The tray (Windows) and menu-bar (macOS) menu gain "Switch every display to…" and a submenu
for each shared display, so you can switch without opening a window. The host on screen is
ticked.

### Why the version jumps to 0.7.0

Under rules 2 and 3 of `docs/versioning.md`: hosts on v0.6.x can no longer pair with an
updated host, and where the settings are, and how they are laid out, has changed.

### Known limitations

- A switch from the tray that fails shows no message; it is logged, and reported if
  diagnostics are allowed.
- Tray items can be chosen whenever a port is set, even if this computer cannot currently
  control that display; such a switch fails.
- Hosts that have never been given a colour may default to a different one than in v0.6.0.
- The macOS DMG uses an ad-hoc signature and is not notarized with an Apple Developer ID,
  so Gatekeeper may ask you to allow it manually.
